Single-cell RNA-seq: mouse enteric neuron atlas

Example report made with Claude and the BRC plugin · P01 Internal Board demo

Author

Bioinformatics Resource Center, Rockefeller University

Published

November 13, 2026

NoteAbout this report

Everything here was produced in a single Claude session with the BRC plugin, which gives Claude access to single-cell datasets hosted by the BRC (here 76 datasets) and tools to query and plot them. The prompts used are shown in each section. The two plots shown live in the P01 board demo are in sections 2 and 3.

Data: public dataset GSE302208 (BRC id GSE302208_ens_atlas_geo_upload): 7,640 mouse enteric neurons, plate-based, 22,511 genes.

1. What’s in the dataset?

“Load the ENS atlas GSE302208 and summarise it: cells, mice and genes per cell by gut region, and by condition.”

What Claude found: 7,640 neurons from 71 mice, from two sources: 2,410 cells from 25 mice in an earlier ENS atlas (labelled ENS_Atlas_2021, all SPF, Uchl1 or Sox10 reporters) and 5,230 cells from 46 mice in the current study across 8 conditions. Depth is high (median ~6,500–6,800 genes per cell in colon and ileum), as expected for plate-based sequencing. The duodenum/jejunum cells are the exception: median 2,836 genes per cell, less than half the other regions, so treat that region with care. Several conditions come from only 3–5 mice.

2. Neuron types and gut region

“Load the ENS atlas GSE302208 and show the UMAP coloured by cell_type_annot.” then “Now colour it by location.”

What Claude found: the authors’ annotation has 19 neuron types in five classes, named by prefix: PSN (putative sensory), PEMN and PIMN (excitatory and inhibitory motor), PIN (interneurons) and PSVN (secretomotor/vasodilator). The largest group is PSN Nmu-hi (877 cells). Colon, ileum and duodenum/jejunum cells mix within most clusters, so the main structure is neuron type rather than gut region, although some clusters lean towards colon (section 4).

3. Piezo2, Nmu and Gdf15

“Show Piezo2, Nmu and Gdf15 as a dot plot by cell_type_annot.” then “Show Gdf15 as a violin plot by cell type.”

What Claude found: the annotation checks out for the two marker genes: Piezo2 is highest in PSN Piezo2-hi, and Nmu is highest in PSN Nmu-hi. Gdf15 is close to zero in every neuron type: few cells express it and the median is zero everywhere. So in this atlas, enteric neurons are not a source of Gdf15, which fits the P01’s focus on GDF15⁺ epithelium (Project 1).

Tip

Absence in one dataset is not proof. These are sorted neurons only, so this says nothing about Gdf15 in epithelium or immune cells. For that, ask the same question of the whole-tissue atlas (GSE301963).

What Claude found: some neuron types are clearly regional. PSN Nmu-hi and PSN Mc4r-hi are much more common in the small intestine (Nmu-hi 16–24% vs 6.5% in colon; Mc4r-hi 7–11% vs 0.8%). PSN Grp-hi, PIN Penk-hi and PIMN Bglap-hi are mostly colonic. Region is mixed with study and condition here (for example, the 2021 atlas cells are colon and SPF only), so check that a difference holds within one study before relying on it.

What the BRC plugin did

Step What you ask What happens behind the scenes
Find data “What single-cell datasets are available?” Lists the 76 scRNA-seq datasets the BRC hosts
Load “Load the ENS atlas GSE302208” Activates the dataset on the BRC server
Summaries “Cells and genes per cell by region”, “% of each neuron type by region” Read-only queries of the cell metadata
Plots “UMAP by cell type”, “dot plot of Piezo2, Nmu, Gdf15”, “violin of Gdf15” The server draws the plots from the full expression data
Report “Put it all in one report” Writes this page

The expression data never leave the BRC server. Claude only sees the summaries and plots it asks for.

WarningBefore you use results like these

The cell-type labels come from the depositors’ annotation; Claude did not re-cluster or re-annotate. Plate-based data, uneven numbers of mice per condition and region–study confounding all limit what can be compared. Treat these as leads, and ask the BRC for a formal analysis.
